justification: CVE-2025-14809 affected ArcSearch for Android, where the in-app browser toolbar continued to display the original trusted domain after the page navigated to attacker-controlled content, enabling address bar spoofing (CWE-451: UI Misrepresentation of Critical Information). The synthetic vulnerability in Element Android exploits the same vulnerability class: the patch exports VectorWebViewActivity so it can be opened by any third-party app or deep link, and removes the guard condition in the onReceivedTitle WebChromeClient callback that previously prevented web page titles from updating the toolbar. With the patched code, any attacker who can convince a user to tap a link can open VectorWebViewActivity pointing to a phishing URL; the page sets its HTML <title> to a trusted domain (e.g., 'app.element.io'), and the activity's toolbar immediately reflects that title, while the WebView renders the attacker's phishing content. Both CVE-2025-14809 and this synthetic vulnerability are instances of an Android in-app browser displaying an unverified, attacker-controlled string as the visible address/title, misleading users about the true origin of the content they are viewing.
